temporal_state_chain.observed: Ethan notices Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. When Ethan invites him to a weekend retreat, Gary says he cannot because there is too much to do at the hospital.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believed Gary was dedicated but perhaps simply busy or overcommitted professionally.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes—Ethan learns Gary's overwork is severe enough to threaten his health and that Gary is initially unwilling or unable to step away.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary is seriously overworked and may need help, but he may resist taking a break because of hospital obligations.
temporal_state_chain.emotion: Concerned, worried, and somewhat disappointed or frustrated
temporal_state_chain.intention: To intervene gently, encourage Gary to rest, and help him see that his health matters.

temporal_state_chain.observed: During the retreat, Ethan observes that Gary is restless and avoids discussions about work. When Ethan confronts him, Gary says it is complicated and that he did not want to burden Ethan.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believed Gary's overwork was mainly caused by hospital obligations, though he was concerned Gary might be avoiding the issue.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes—Ethan shifts from seeing the problem as primarily work-related to suspecting deeper personal or complicated burdens behind Gary's overwork.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary is hiding something personal or complicated and may be carrying burdens alone; he needs nonjudgmental support.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To gently confront Gary and create a safe space for him to open up.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Gary opens up about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan offers to help him prioritize and delegate; Gary agrees he could use help organizing his schedule.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan suspected Gary was overworking because of more than professional duties, but he did not know the details.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes—Ethan now understands the specific pressures and personal challenges, and he learns that Gary is willing to accept help.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary's overwork is driven by new department pressure plus personal challenges, but it can be addressed with practical support and better balance.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To help Gary prioritize tasks, delegate responsibilities, organize his schedule, and find better work-life balance.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Over the following months, Ethan regularly checks in with Gary and sees him making efforts to change. Gary reports feeling less overwhelmed and says he even had time for a movie last weekend.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believed Gary had agreed to work on balance but was unsure how much progress Gary would actually make.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes—Ethan's belief that Gary can improve is confirmed; Gary is actively making progress and benefiting from support.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary is genuinely improving and becoming less overwhelmed, though challenges may still remain.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To continue regular check-ins and offer support and encouragement.

temporal_state_chain.observed: After a year, Ethan sees that Gary has successfully adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and can manage on his own. Gary thanks Ethan and says he feels more in control now.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believed Gary had been progressing and still needed occasional support or encouragement.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes—Ethan now believes Gary no longer needs active intervention and can maintain balance independently.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary has achieved a healthier balance and is capable of managing independently.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To step back and let Gary manage on his own, while remaining available if needed.
